content.overview: Article 323A empowers Parliament by law to provide for the adjudication or trial by administrative tribunals of disputes and complaints with respect to recruitment and conditions of service of persons appointed to public services and posts in connection with the affairs of the Union or of any State or of any local or other authority within the territory of India or under the control of the Government of India or of any corporation owned or controlled by the Government. The law may provide for a hierarchy of tribunals, specify powers and procedure (including limited application of the CPC/Evidence Act), and exclude the jurisdiction of all courts except the Supreme Court under Article 136 with respect to such disputes — subject to the Constitution and judicial interpretation on the scope of exclusion (including High Court jurisdiction under Articles 226/227).
content.glance: Parliament may by law create administrative tribunals for service disputes (Union/State/local/government-controlled bodies). May provide hierarchy, procedure, and exclusion of courts except SC under Art 136 — subject to constitutional limits on ouster.
content.study:
Article 323A (42nd Amendment) is the constitutional basis for administrative tribunals (e.g. Central Administrative Tribunal):
1. Subject-matter: recruitment and conditions of service of public servants (Union, State, local authorities, government-controlled corporations).
2. Parliament may provide hierarchy, jurisdiction, powers, and procedure.
3. May exclude jurisdiction of all courts except the Supreme Court under Article 136 — but complete ouster of High Court judicial review has been constrained by basic-structure/judicial-review jurisprudence (e.g. L. Chandra Kumar).

Examination: service disputes; parliamentary law; hierarchy; limited court exclusion; Art 136 preserved; judicial review limits on ouster.

sections.heading: Key elements
sections.body:
1. Parliament may by law provide administrative tribunals for service-related disputes.
2. Covers Union, State, local and government-controlled bodies’ public services/posts.
3. Law may provide hierarchy, powers, procedure, and (subject to constitutional limits) exclusion of courts except SC under Art 136.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does Article 323A provide?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article 323A empowers Parliament by law to provide for the adjudication by administrative tribunals of disputes and complaints with respect to recruitment and conditions of service of persons appointed to public services and posts in connection with the affairs of the Union or of any State or of any local or other authority or government-controlled corporation. The law may provide for the hierarchy, jurisdiction, powers and procedure of such tribunals and may exclude the jurisdiction of all courts except the Supreme Court under Article 136 with respect to such disputes, subject to the Constitution and the limits on ouster of judicial review recognised by the Supreme Court.
